summary: Firefox substantially improved platform media acceleration across Linux, Windows, Android, and macOS. Linux Vulkan Video support now covers more hardware and FFmpeg configurations, caches devices and codec capabilities, fails cleanly when required functions are unavailable, and avoids unsupported H.264 cases; Windows Media Foundation avoids risky realtime VPX hardware encoding and rejects invalid odd-width inputs; Apple VideoToolbox handles planar, mapped, and NVImage frames more safely. HDR metadata from hardware-decoded video is now passed to the compositor, improving brightness and color after HDR playback, while additional fixes address Wayland HDR restoration, chroma location, MediaCapabilities codec checks, content-protection synchronization, and Media Engine stream handling.
